第 13 章 Dealing with Uncertainty应对不确定性

Mathias Meyer / 马蒂亚斯·迈耶

— 第 46 页 —

As a manager, you make decisions—lots of them. Many of them are small, usually quick and easy to make. There might be frameworks in place at your company that help you. For instance, when someone comes and asks you for a raise, a career and salary framework guides you through the process. Finding a yes or no answer and a good explanation is simple enough in those cases.

作为经理，你做决策——很多决策。很多是小决策，通常快速且容易做。公司可能有框架帮你。比如有人来找你要求加薪，职业和薪资框架会引导你走流程。在这些情况下，找一个是或否的答案和好的解释足够简单。

However, there are many decisions for which you'll be faced with imperfect information. Your view as an engineering manager is limited. Given the many parties that you interact with every day, you have many perspectives to take into account. Some of these will be conflicting, even opposing. Others will contain only a shred of the real picture.

然而，有很多决策你面对的信息是不完美的。作为工程经理，你的视野有限。考虑到你每天打交道的各方，你有很多视角需要纳入考量。有些是相互冲突的，甚至对立的。另一些只包含真实图景的一小部分。

You can delegate decision making to your team as much as possible. But you won't prevent the most uncomfortable decisions from landing on your (virtual) desk at some point.

你可以尽可能把决策授权给团队。但你无法阻止最让人不舒服的决策在某个时候落到你的（虚拟）办公桌上。

It's easy to become stuck in these situations because you don't know how to balance the different perspective. You want to be sure that you've considered all perspectives. You want the solution to address all concerns equally. You want to talk to one more person.

在这些情况下很容易卡住，因为你不知道怎么平衡不同的视角。你想确保自己考虑了所有视角。你希望方案能平等解决所有关切。你想再找一个人聊聊。

Every manager (including me!) has been in this position at some point, and they can very much relate to how you feel. Making decisions in the face of an increasing amount of uncertainty can be terrifying. The higher up you move in your management career, the more uncertainty you'll be faced with. Information will be sparse, and it will be limited in detail.

每个经理（包括我！）都在某个时刻处于这个位置，他们非常能理解你的感受。在越来越多的不确定性面前做决策可能是可怕的。你在管理生涯中升得越高，面临的不确定性就越多。信息会很稀少，细节也有限。

Here's the flip side that every manager also understands: you're afraid to make a decision. You're afraid to make a decision that your team won't like. You're afraid the team disagrees. You're afraid that you're making the wrong decision and that you'll be exposed as not knowing what you're doing.

每个经理也都理解的另一面是：你害怕做决策。你害怕做一个团队不喜欢的决策。你害怕团队不同意。你害怕自己做了错误的决策，会被暴露为不知道自己在干什么。

— 第 47 页 —

Making decisions with imperfect information is never easy. You're asked to predict a future that you know nothing about based on very little knowledge. But not making one will lead to your team not knowing what to do or where to go. Eventually, the team will burn out and leave.

在信息不完美的情况下做决策从来不容易。你被要求基于很少的知识预测一个你一无所知的未来。但不做决策会导致团队不知道该做什么、该往哪走。最终，团队会倦怠离开。

As difficult as this is, you'll need to get used to having to make these kinds of decisions. Some folks will defer these questions to their boss, asking them to make the call in their stead. This can work in smaller teams. But it means that you're not doing your job.

尽管这很难，你需要习惯做这种决策。有些人会把这些问题推给老板，让老板替他们做决定。这在小团队里可能行得通。但这意味着你没在做你的工作。

It's tempting to think that you always want to make the correct decision. But I offer a subtly different take: it's important to make a good decision, not always the correct one. A good decision is one that you're making for the right reasons. It's not a decision that everyone must like or agree with.

人很容易认为你总是要做正确的决策。但我有一个微妙不同的看法：做一个好决策很重要，不总是正确的决策。好决策是你出于正确理由做出的决策。它不是一个每个人都必须喜欢或同意的决策。

How do you get there? Here's a little framework that can guide you through the process:

怎么做到呢？这里有一个小框架可以引导你走过这个过程：

Start defining the problems and goals先定义问题和目标

Any decision that doesn't have a good set of goals and problem definitions attached to it will likely not get the buy-in you might be hoping for. There are decisions for which this isn't possible due to confidentiality reasons. But for most decisions, be clear on the goals. This helps avoid bikeshedding, where people argue about the implementation or a detail rather than first reaching agreement on whether they really need a shed.

任何没有明确目标和问题定义的决策，很可能得不到你希望的支持。有些决策因为保密原因做不到这一点。但对大多数决策来说，目标要清晰。这有助于避免自行车棚效应——人们争论实现细节而不是先就是否真的需要一个棚达成一致。

Collect information from multiple sources从多个来源收集信息

Talk to several people in your company to get a fair overview of what people think about the problem at hand. Don't stretch it out for eternity though. Set yourself a time limit or list out the people who you think would have the strongest opinions and would be affected the most.

和公司里几个人聊聊，公平地了解大家对当前问题的看法。但不要无限期地拖下去。给自己设一个时间限制，或者列出你认为意见最强、受影响最大的人。

Outline the options列出选项

Outlining more than one option that you've considered in your decision making makes it clear to people that you've tried to make a fair decision that considers multiple angles, including theirs.

列出你在决策中考虑过的多个选项，让人们清楚你试图做一个公平的、考虑了多个角度（包括他们的角度）的决策。

Be cognizant of the risks意识到风险

Think about what consequences the decision might have and what risks you associate with it. This is a good way to go beyond your fears and gut feeling and really think about the best and the worst that could happen, and anything in between.

想想这个决策可能有什么后果、你认为它有什么风险。这是一个好方法，可以超越你的恐惧和直觉，真正思考最好和最坏的情况，以及中间的任何情况。

— 第 48 页 —

Consider doing experiments instead of making decisions考虑用做实验代替做决策

Decisions seem more difficult to make because they tend to appear valid for an infinite amount of time. You can reduce this by considering a decision as an experiment that expires after a period of time. This could be one month, or three, or six. After that time, you'll revisit the decision to see whether it's turned out the way you thought.

决策看起来更难做，是因为它们似乎无限期有效。你可以通过把决策看作一个有期限的实验来减轻这种感觉。期限可以是一个月、三个月或六个月。之后，你再回顾这个决策，看看结果是否如你所想。
